Current programme and course evidence support Dutch, Arabic and English instruction.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target is Arabic Language and Culture. Of the two current formal majors, Major Arabische studies directly continues the programme’s intensive Arabic-language sequence, Arabic-source work, Cairo semester and Arabic-language thesis. Major Middle Eastern Studies explicitly ends language acquisition after year 1 and is therefore less representative of the named generic bachelor. The route was selected before assessing UCR fit.

programmes.label: Arabische Taal en Cultuur at University of Amsterdam

exception.reason: Three independently organised directions were tested. Arabic language, literature and source-based cultural study fails because UCR offers no Arabic acquisition sequence and no course in Arabic literature, Arabic media or Arabic-source interpretation. Middle Eastern history, society and culture has genuine comparative history, sociology, archaeology, heritage and humanities methods, but no sustained Arab-world, Middle East or Islam sequence. Middle Eastern politics, contemporary debates and conflict has international-relations, comparative-politics, law and conflict frameworks, but no region-centred political history, Gulf politics, religion-and-politics or contemporary Arab-society formation. In every direction, extending adjacent methods to 23 non-PPD courses would change the object of study to generic global humanities or international studies. The missing Arabic-language and regional content are academic substance rather than professional qualification, so no complete UCR response is claimed.
exception.curriculumContext: The selected Arabic Studies specialisation closes 60+60+60 and is kept separate from Middle Eastern Studies. It includes the compulsory 30-EC Cairo semester, a 12-EC thesis and 30 EC of genuine free profiling. Diagnostic test 109121025Y and recurring tutoring 12102A025Y are mandatory zero-credit formation and do not increase the total. Current programme and course evidence support Dutch, Arabic and English instruction.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions or outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and Fall-2026-start availability. MCCCOMM112 teaches introductory Dutch, not Arabic; HCBCOGN312 studies language processing, acquisition and bilingualism, but is not language instruction. MCCLITR111/112/211/212/312, MCCCOMM211 and MCCMEDI111/112/311/312 provide real literary, linguistic, rhetorical and media-analysis methods, but their documented content does not teach Arabic literature, Arabic sociolinguistics, Arabic media or Arabic-source interpretation. GOSHIST111 and GOSHIST211 provide modern and imperial history; GOSSOCI111/212/214/311 provide social theory and qualitative/decolonial analysis; MCCHEAM112 includes isolated archaeological examples in Türkiye and Sudan, and MCCHEAM211 studies West African art and heritage. None provides a sustained Arab-world, Middle East or Islamic-history sequence. GOSPOLI112/212/313, GOSLAWJ212/213 and BENECON211 provide comparative politics, international relations, conflict, law and macroeconomic frameworks, but no course centres Middle Eastern politics, Gulf states, Islam and politics, or contemporary Arab societies. No workbook row teaches Arabic, Arabic reading/writing or a Middle East area-studies spine. Academic feasibility therefore fails before course scheduling, so no 24-course programme or UCR-credit comparison is fabricated.

candidateAssessment.concept: Arabic language, literature and source-based cultural study
candidateAssessment.assessment: UCR provides literary interpretation, stylistics, psycholinguistics, rhetoric and media analysis, but no Arabic acquisition, reading or writing, Arabic literature, Arabic media, Arabic sociolinguistics or Arabic-source research. Generic language and humanities methods cannot supply the language and cultural object that organise this direction.

candidateAssessment.concept: Middle Eastern history, society and culture
candidateAssessment.assessment: Comparative history, empire, sociology, archaeology, heritage and qualitative research are genuine analytic foundations. Their documented content does not provide sustained study of Arab cultural history, Islam, Middle Eastern political history, Arab societies or regional cultural texts. A full curriculum would become general global humanities rather than a defensible Middle Eastern regional programme.

candidateAssessment.concept: Middle Eastern politics, contemporary debates and conflict
candidateAssessment.assessment: International relations, comparative politics, public international law and peace-and-conflict study supply transferable frameworks. They do not teach Middle Eastern political history, Gulf politics, religion and politics, regional news or contemporary Arab social debates, so expanding them to a full programme would become generic international studies.
